item.title: Germany’s ‘Firewall’ Against the Far Right Is Being Tested as Never Before
item.description: A blowout win by the far-right Alternative for Germany party in a state election has revealed a split among voters about whether to uphold a decades-old strategy for sidelining extremists.

item.title: After Victory in German State, Far Right Needs Help to Take Power
item.description: The Alternative for Germany, or AfD, does not have a straightforward path to governing Saxony-Anhalt, but a small populist party could clear the way.

item.media:credit: Liesa Johannssen/Reuters
item.media:description: Tino Chrupalla, left, and Alice Weidel, right, co-leaders of the far-right Alternative for Germany party, with Ulrich Siegmund, center, the party’s leader in Saxony-Anhalt, in Berlin on Monday.

item.title: AfD Victory in Saxony-Anhalt Sends a Signal to Europe
item.description: A vote in eastern Germany has given fresh momentum to hard-right parties hoping to win elections elsewhere on the continent next year, analysts said.
